title: fix(driver-sql): MySQL autonumber issues duplicate numbers when the first rows of an object are written concurrently
body:
epic:#3814#1 · os-zhuang · session_01QUs3BrVu5TqwtmuhsjdEvM
Filing gate: ③ maintainer-dispatched task (child of #3814). Maintainer, (2026-11-08, 16:25 UTC): 「继续，现在派第二批」 (gate 1 after the card 0 inventory, cloud#3868 comment 6723322368).

Single-node defect S3, found by card 0 of #3814 (cloud#3868 comment 6723322368, V1b). Maintainer ruling D2 (2026-11-08, 16:25 UTC): 「现在修，按普通 bug 卡」. This is a single-node bug fix, so it is NOT bound by #3814's R3.

## Problem (measured, MySQL 8.0)
On a new object, concurrent creates produced duplicate autonumbers every run: two processes gave 11-18 duplicates plus up to 21 `ER_LOCK_DEADLOCK` create errors, and a single process at concurrency 16 also gave 8/8/0 duplicates. A warm sequence passes. There is no unique index on the autonumber column. The likely cause (not proven) is that a deadlock rolls back past the savepoint during the cold seed. Postgres 16 passes the same probe (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`). The probe scripts are in project files `issue-3868/`.

## Do
1. Root-cause the cold-seed path in driver-sql for MySQL and make it atomic (for example, seed the sequence row with an insert-ignore before the locking read, and retry the whole issue on deadlock).
2. Consider the unique index the autonumber contract implies; if adding it is a schema change for existing installs, say so in the PR and keep it to new objects unless the migration is safe.
3. Tests: the concurrent cold-seed probe on MySQL gives 1..N with no duplicates; Postgres unchanged.

## Done when
PR merged; concurrent first writes on MySQL never duplicate an autonumber.
